clock: t is seconds since the first hook; hook records keep only the ps rows of the rig's sleep processes, taken inside the hook; a transcript line's t is the rig's poll time, so take write order from the line's own timestamp
note: Claude launches a one-agent background workflow (the agent runs `sleep 40.07`) and the turn ends; the launch turn's Stop lists it as `type: workflow`. The workflow completes: its agent's SubagentStop, then Claude's `queue-operation` enqueue row (completed, the launch's task id and tool-use id, plus `<result>` and `<diagnostics>`), then a report turn whose Stop lists nothing. Write order by Claude's own row timestamp: end row 17:00:28.690Z; the report turn's UserPromptSubmit hook is 41 ms later. The fixture `t` of a transcript line is the rig's later poll time (margin 6 ms), not its write time.
